reply.title: Squashing Numbers with the Logistic Curve
reply.story: When modeling probabilities or neural networks, we often need to take any number from negative infinity to positive infinity and map it neatly between zero and one. A linear scale cannot do this because it grows without bound. By exploring the logistic curve, we see how an exponential function in the denominator naturally creates a smooth S-shaped barrier. As the input grows very large, the denominator dominates and forces the output toward one. As it becomes very negative, the output shrinks toward zero.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any input into a bounded range between zero and one. Adjust the steepness parameter to see how sharply the transition occurs.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness slider to change how fast the curve transitions from zero to one. Observe the marker and readouts update instantly.
